title: Universal cohomology vanishing over a binary closed union
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian topological space (ascending chains of open subsets stabilize), let $Z,W$ be closed subsets and let $q\geq0$. Suppose $H^q(Z,G)=0$ for every abelian sheaf $G$ on $Z$ and $H^q(W,G)=0$ for every abelian sheaf $G$ on $W$, with the subspace topologies [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology]. Then $H^q(Z\cup W,F)=0$ for every abelian sheaf $F$ on $Z\cup W$ with its subspace topology.

source.place: Proposition 02UZ (cohomology-proposition-vanishing-Noetherian), component-reduction paragraph; Lemma 02UV; Modules Lemma 02UT

proof.text: Put T = Z union W with its subspace topology and U = T minus the inverse image of Z. The inclusion T into X is a closed embedding, T is Noetherian, and U is open. Write D for the closed complement of U and C for its closure. Since U is contained in the inverse image of W, which is closed, C is contained there too. The double subtype maps D into Z and C into W are closed embeddings: composing with the subtype embeddings of Z and W into X gives the composite of two closed subtype embeddings.

Apply [lem-sc-noetherian-open-closed-cohomology-sequence] to T, U and F. Obtain its short exact sequence S with middle term F, right term the closed pushforward from D of the pullback of F, and left term whose degree-q cohomology is isomorphic to that of a sheaf G on C.

Push the pullback of F on D along D into Z and apply hZ. Comparison [lem-sc-cohomology-closed-immersion-pushforward] first for D into Z and then for D into T gives zero cohomology for S.X3. Push G along C into W and apply hW; the same comparison gives zero cohomology for G on C. The cohomology isomorphism from the preceding step gives zero cohomology for S.X1. In each comparison transfer subsingletonness between the small Ext model of the hypotheses and the standard model using Mathlib Abelian.Ext.chgUniv.

For any degree-q Ext class x of F, its image in S.X3 is zero. Mathlib Abelian.Ext.covariant_sequence_exact₂ gives a preimage y in S.X1. That group is zero, so y and then x are zero. Thus the cohomology of F is a subsingleton, hence a zero abelian group. This is the long exact sequence for [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology], including degree zero. Transfer the result back to the small Ext model using Abelian.Ext.chgUniv.

theorem cohomology_vanishing_of_closed_union
    (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] [NoetherianSpace X]
    (Z W : Closeds X) (q : ℕ)
    (hZ : ∀ G : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology (Z : Set X)) AddCommGrpCat.{u},
      IsZero (Sheaf.H' G q (⊤ : Opens (Z : Set X))))
    (hW : ∀ G : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology (W : Set X)) AddCommGrpCat.{u},
      IsZero (Sheaf.H' G q (⊤ : Opens (W : Set X))))
    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology ((Z ⊔ W : Closeds X) : Set X))
      AddCommGrpCat.{u}) :
    IsZero (Sheaf.H' F q (⊤ : Opens ((Z ⊔ W : Closeds X) : Set X)))
